Abdul Khalek and others
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's bazar and others
full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the predecessor of the petitioners, Noor Ahmed as plaintiff, instituted Other Suit No. 104 of 1994 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, against the opposite parties, as defendant, for declaration of title and declaring that B.S. khatian Nos. 1, 3 and 195 are wrong, ineffective and the plaintiff is not bound by said wrong khatian, stating inter alia, that the suit property is khas land of the government. Predecessor of the petitioner namely, Noor Ahmed obtained permanent settlement of the suit land from the government vide Settlement Case No. 287/1977-78 by a registered lease deed No. 5000 dated 04.07.1979. After settlement the government opened a separate khatian No. 445 in the name of Noor Ahmed and delivered possession of the same showing position by a trace map. Predecessor of the petitioners had been possessing the suit land on payment of rent to the government and after two years of settlement he constructed a house thereon and after 15 years constructed some shop houses on a portion of the lease hold land measuring 24 sataks, but concern employees of the government wrongly included and shown excess land in the trace map. Predecessor of the petitioner when went to the local Tahsil Office for payment of rent for the suit land, concerned Tahasilder refused to accept the rent on the ground that B.S. khatian for the suit land has not been recorded in the name of Noor Ahmed. Thereafter, on enquiry he came to know that the suit property has been recorded in the name of defendant. The said record in the name of the defendant is wrong, baseless and ineffective and by the said wrong recording, title of the plaintiff has became clouded, hence the present suit for declaration. 

 4. The defendants in the manner aforesaid, by acquiring title in the property have been possessing the same with the knowledge of all and present B.S. khatian No. 195 finally stand recorded in their names, but in B.S. record quantum of land under R.S. plot No. 3309 has been recorded as 1.00 acre instead of 1.09 acres, 9 sataks recorded in khatian No. 1 as khas land of the government. R.S plot No. 3309 corresponds present B.S. plot Nos. 4910, 4914, 4930 and 4915. The land of the defendants recorded in B.S. plot No. 4910, 4914 and 4930 of B.S. khatian No. 195 measuring one acres. Remaining land recorded in B.S. plot Nos. 4914 and 4930 and a portion of the land under aforesaid two plots fell in road and graveyard. 20 sataks of land under B.S. plot No. 4910 of khatian No. 542 stands recorded in the name of Abdur Rahman and others. Therefore, there was no remaining land to be leased out by the government in favour of Noor Ahmed. The trace map of the plaintiff overlapped the land of the defendants. 

 5. Moreover, government khas land ought to have leased out to the landless people for cultivation, but the plaintiff is not a landless man and the property in question is not a paddy land. The plaintiff in connivance with the officials of the government managed to create the lease showing excess land in the attached trace map overlapping the land of the defendants. The suit is false and liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Md. Zahedul Bari, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the property measuring 24 sataks were khas land of the government. Predecessor of the petitioner, Noor Ahmed obtained settlement of the same from the government vide Settlement Case No. 287/77-78 and leasehold land of the plaintiff is under R.S. plot No. 3309/01 measuring 13 sataks and plot No. 3309/02 measuring 11 sataks, totalling 24 sataks and by a trace map and opening a separate khatian in the name of Noor Ahmed, possession of the leasehold property was delivered and since then, the petitioners right from their predecessor have been continuously possessing the same on payment of rent to the government. He further submits that all the P.Ws corroborating each other deposed before the trial court that the petitioners are in possession of the suit property and using the same as their homestead and shop house. Though the present B.S. khatian wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants, possession of the plaintiff has not been disturbed in any way but for such wrong recording title of the plaintiff has become clouded for which the plaintiff filed the instant suit. He further submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court while dismissing the suit and the appeal most unfortunately failed to consider evidences led by the plaintiff both oral and documentary and relying on the evidence of the defendants dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. 

 10. Mr. Kamal ul Alam, learned senior Advocate with Mr. Masud ul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submit that R.S. plot No. 3309 contains only 1.09 acres of land which was settled by the zaminder in favour of defendant No. 3 and others and there is no dispute that R.S. plot No. 3309 corresponds B.S. plot No. 4910, 4914, 4930 and 4915 under B.S khatian No. 195 and recorded in the name of the defendants. Therefore, in B.S. khatian No. 195, plot Nos. 4910, 4914, 4930 and 4915 there was no khas land to be leased out by the government in favour of anybody. 

 11. It is also argued that it is nobody's case that R.S. plot No. 3309 is khas land of the government, but the property under said plot is the private property owned by the defendants in suit. Therefore, the defendant No. 1, government has had no right or title to lease out the property under plot No. 3309 to the plaintiff. It is true that a quantum of .09 sataks land recorded in the name of the government under B.S. khatian No. 1 as khas land. The said quantum of land fell under Roads and Highway and a graveyard adjacent to the road. He further submits that trace map prepared showing position of land settled in favour of the plaintiff is 36 ½  sataks whereas 24 sataks of land as admitted in the plaint was settled in favour of the plaintiff instead of 09 sataks only which is now under road and graveyard. 

 14. It is the case of the plaintiff that they obtained settlement of 24 sataks land under MRR khatian No. 1 vide Settlement Case No. 287/77-78 from the government and since then they have been possessing the suit property on payment of rent. Dispute between the parties that the property shown in trace map attached to the lease deed showing position of the property settled in favour of plaintiff overlapped the property of the defendants and there was no such quantum of land to be leased out to the plaintiff MRR khatian No. 1 contain only .38 sataks of land, out of which the plaintiff claimed 24 sataks, but the trace map shows the quantum of land is 36 ½  sataks, covered by R.S. plot No. 3309 and the said plot corresponds to B.S. plot Nos. 4910, 4914, 4930 and 4915 under B.S. khatian No. 195. Therefore, it can be easily said that the property under B.S. khatian No. 195 are not the khas land of the government. The government has been made party in the suit, but they did not contest the suit or claim that the property in question was khas land of the government and settled the same in favour of the plaintiff. MRR khatian No. 94 shows that plot No. 3309 contain 1.09 acres and B.S. khatian No. 195 contains only 1.00 acre. According to defence case remaining .09 sataks land recorded as khas land of the government under B.S. khatian No.1 and they do not claim such land to be their private land. B.S. khatian No. 1 contains only .38 sataks land, out of which earlier the government leased out 20 sataks of land to one Abdur Rahman and others. After leasing out 20 sataks to Abdur Rahman and others their remains only 16 ½ sataks of land. On the said land there is a pathway under Roads and Highway and a public graveyard as contended by the defendant in their written statement as well as on oath. Therefore, there was no land to be settled in favour of the plaintiff. 

 16. In the instant suit the plaintiff is to prove first, that the property settled in his favour is the khas land of the government and then to prove that the specific property was settled to him with definite boundary and possession of the same were delivered to him. But in the instant case the plaintiff has failed to prove identification of the settled land and delivery of possession of the same to him, as the trace map showing position of the property does not tally with the quantum of land settled by the registered lease deed of the year 1978. As such, the court below rightly dismissed the suit as no court can pass a decree in respect of unspecified and unidentified property as per law. The plaintiff sought a declaration to the effect that B.S. khatian Nos. 1, 3 and 195 are false, illegal, wrong, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff as well as on the suit property but he failed to give any specification as to what quantum of land out of 24 sataks wrongly entered in those khatians under which plot.
